newsitem.title: USA: US House panel okays interim nuclear waste storage.
newsitem.headline: US House panel okays interim nuclear waste storage.

text.p: A U.S. House panel Thursday approved a bill to make the federal government build a temporary dump in Nevada that would be ready to start accepting nuclear waste in January 2002.

The House Commerce Energy and Power subcommittee passed the bill, which has been pushed by the nuclear power industry, on a 21-3 vote after rejecting several amendments offered by Massachusetts Democrat Edward Markey.
Markey told the panel that the White House repeated to him earlier in the day that President Clinton would veto the bill in its current form.

The White House has said the bill to build a temporary waste dump in Nevada would prejudge Nevada's Yucca Mountain as the permanent waste dump site, and would detract from the effort to build the permanent site.

But Subcommittee Chairman Dan Schaefer, a Colorado Republican, said the bill would provide for the permanent repository, while seeing that the federal government meet its obligations to start accepting waste from nuclear reactors.
"Construction of a permanent repository has always been our ultimate goal, and this should be the goal of our efforts here today," Schaefer said.
